from_quote: DRAFT proof-method concept; this special-case argument was independently checked by w355 and assigned referee w356. No novelty or full KLS claim. Let d>=2, K=(d+1)(d+2), X be uniform on Delta_d={x_i>=0,sum_i x_i<=1}, m=(1,...,1)/(d+1), Sigma=(I-J/(d+1))/K with J the all-ones matrix, A=Sigma^(-1/2), Y=A(X-m), a=sqrt(2K), and v=Ae_1/a. Put Z=Proj_(v-perp)Y, T=<v,Y> and S=sum_(j=2)^d X_j. Given 0<epsilon<1, choose a nonzero smooth eta supported in (epsilon/4,epsilon/2) and put f(Y)=eta(S) sin(pi T/(a(1-S))). Each such f has finite full energy, E[f|Z]=0, E Var(f|Z)=E eta(S)^2/2 and E|partial_v f|^2=(pi^2/(2a^2)) E[eta(S)^2/(1-S)^2]. Its directional quotient is at least (2K/pi^2)(1-epsilon)^2, and the support has positive probability. Letting epsilon go to zero proves that the optimal directional conditional coefficient is 2K/pi^2. This card records the localized admissible witness method, rather than duplicating the common simplex-constants card. It does not bound the full-gradient KLS constant.

from_quote: DRAFT independently checked special-case formula: w355's full-packet audit checked Section 5; w356 kept its d=2,k=2 specialization. No novelty or full KLS claim. Let d>=2, K=(d+1)(d+2), X be uniform on Delta_d={x_i>=0,sum_i x_i<=1}, m=(1,...,1)/(d+1), Sigma=(I-J/(d+1))/K with J the all-ones matrix, A=Sigma^(-1/2), Y=A(X-m), a=sqrt(2K), and v=Ae_1/a. Put Z=Proj_(v-perp)Y, T=<v,Y> and S=sum_(j=2)^d X_j. For every integer k>=1 put t=1-S, f(Y)=T t^k and M_p=(p+1)! d!/(d+p)!. Then E[f|Z]=0, E Var(f|Z)=(K/6) M_(2k+2), E|partial_v f|^2=M_(2k), and E|grad f|^2=[1+k^2(d-1)/(3(d+1))] M_(2k). Thus the exact directional quotient is R_(d,k)=(K/6)(2k+2)(2k+3)/[(d+2k+1)(d+2k+2)], while the full-gradient quotient is R_(d,k)/[1+k^2(d-1)/(3(d+1))]. The extra factor is the transverse gradient cost: grad_Y S is perpendicular to v and has squared norm 2(d-1)/((d+1)K). For d=2,k=2 these give variance 1/2, directional energy 1/3 and full energy 13/27. The family generalizes the separately submitted triangle witness and explicitly preserves all gradient terms.
